newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia sees 97 inflation between 8.8 and 9.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia sees 97 inflation between 8.8 and 9.0 pct.

text.p: Slovenian 1997 inflation is expected to be between 8.8 and nine percent compared to last year's 8.8 percent, Marjan Senjur, Minister for Economic Relations and Development, said on Wednesday.
"We forecast this year's inflation will be between 8.8 and 9.0 percent," Senjur told a news conference.
Senjur said inflation was expected to stabilise at four to five percent by the year 2000.
Earlier this month Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said he expected 1997 inflation to be slightly lower or unchanged from last year.
"Although monthly inflation in April exceeded the average, we do not expect such increases in future months so the target will be attainable," Senjur said.
April monthly inflation rose to two percent from 0.3 percent in March, mainly due to a nine percent rise in petrol prices. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
